Params.Value: Stoppered squid-dark ink. The quartermasters take payment in it; the scribes never seem to run out.
A toxic chill spreads through the body.
Heat blooms outward in a violent flash.
Warm to the touch; crumbles with a spark. (heat, volatile)
Slow, greasy, eager to burn. (combustible, viscous)
A slow warmth lingers on the tongue. (heat, sweet)
Rimed fronds that ache the fingertips. (cold)
Cracks with a deep, patient chill; sets like mortar. (cold, binding)
Stings the nose; hums faintly against the jar. (corrosive, conductive)
Hairs rise near its severed end. (conductive)
Harvested from something that bit first. (toxic)
Clinging tar with a sour reek. (toxic, viscous)
Beats faintly. Tastes of nothing much. (vital, sweet)
Hard as a knuckle; sets like mortar. (binding)
Do not shake. Do not warm. (volatile, combustible)
A pale seed, faintly sweet-smelling, the size of a fingernail. Plant it in soft ground.
A warm golden grain that never quite cools. Plant it in soft ground.
Crisp and orange and honest about it. Grown, not made.
Cool mist rises from the pages. You learn Conjure Rain.
The rite of rain is already yours.
A damp-smelling tome whose ink never quite dries. Its pages describe how to call small, polite rainclouds down onto growing things.
A sheaf of grain that glows faintly warm, even at night.
Caustic green liquid hisses against your skin.
Static crackles across your skin and hair stands on end.
An ice-cold draught freezes you from the inside.
Cool water, all the way down.
Sharp pain blooms — your wounds reopen.
Bitter ash coats your tongue — your skin hardens against future fire.
The bitter tonic neutralizes the poison.
A warm light floods through you, purging all afflictions.
The tonic sends a quicksilver rush through the body.
Forearms like bridge cables. The ring of the forge follows them around.
Measures you with a glance and starts thinking in buckles and plates.
Smells of forty herbs at once. Knows which twelve could kill you.
Ink-stained fingers, a shelf of humming grimoires, and prices to match.
Sacks, jars, bundles, barrels. If it keeps on a shelf, they stock it.
An old soul grown half into the moss. Keeps a kettle on for travelers.
Sun-cured and patient. They say the dunes talk to those who stop hurrying.
Fingers stained green and black. Knows every leaf that kills and every leaf that saves.
Tends a lamp older than the ruins around it. Remembers what the stones forgot.
A snapjaw warband banner-blade, notched from a hundred raids. Heavier than it looks; meaner than it needs to be.
Soft silver-veined leaves that close when it rains. The herbalists strip them gently; the rotlings just eat the whole plant.
compass stone pointing north toward the Ruins of Sparkwright
compass stone pointing east toward the Saltglass Dunes
compass stone pointing south toward the Verdant Rotbog

You study the faded ink carefully. The rite of water purification takes shape in your mind.
You study the diagrams of force and fracture. The mending rite settles into your hands.
You trace the warding sigils with your eyes. The kindle rite sparks to life in your memory.
Flame-script blazes across the page. The kindle rite burns itself into your mind.
You already know the kindle rite.
Water-words ripple across the vellum. The quench rite flows into your memory.
You already know the quench rite.
The pages ignite as you read, yet do not burn. The conflagration rite sears itself into your will.
You already know the conflagration rite.
Crystalline glyphs bite your fingertips. The ice lance rite chills into your mind.
You already know the ice lance rite.
Corrosive ink hisses as you read. The acid spray rite eats its way into your mind.
You already know the acid spray rite.
Static crackles across the vellum. The arc bolt rite sparks into your memory.
You already know the arc bolt rite.
Frost lances spiral from the margins. The rime nova rite buries itself in your will.
You already know the rime nova rite.
Thunder rolls from the open pages. The thunderclap rite booms itself into your will.
You already know the thunderclap rite.
A vein of embers traces the page. The ember vein rite burns itself into your will.
You already know the ember vein rite.
Warm script flickers in the margins. You learn kindle flame.
The page exhales a dry wind. You learn drying breeze.
Steady embers glow between the lines. You learn hearthwarm.
Condensation beads across the page. You learn conjure water.
A biting draft slips from the pages. You learn chill draft.
The ink brightens to a cleansing sheen. You learn ward gleam.
The whetstone angles, the draw-stroke counts -- the honing pattern settles into your hands.
Overlap the plates like river-scale, the notes say. You see how it carries the blow.
The tailoring lines are drawn for someone who plans to be missed. You take the pattern.
A seam of light-hoarding quartz. It hums faintly when you stand close.
Crystallized white salt threaded through the limestone. The dead are said to hate it.
Dark ore that rings like a struck bell when chipped. The Rot Choir prizes it.
Thunder pools in the gutter of the page. The storm anvil is yours to bring down.
You already know the storm anvil.
The bolt hangs in the margin, refusing to fall. You learn to hold it there.
You already know the hanging bolt.
The page fogs and clears. Water and fire, held together just long enough.
Condensation beads, then hisses away. What soaks you can also shield you.
You already know the scalding veil.
The page holds a single instruction: put the charge down, and let it find its own way.
Frost creeps from the spine as you read. What is frozen is not armoured — it is brittle.
The page is cold and very quiet. You learn how to make a heart forget to hurry.
Green rot flowers across the margin and eats the gilding. The bloom takes root in your hands.
A coin is pressed into the page, worn smooth on both faces. Whatever is owed, it pays.
One word, written far too many times. Reading it once is enough to leave things smaller.
Two columns, in two different inks. You learn which side of the ledger to stand on.
Runs overhead and underfoot. Charge takes it and keeps going.
Salt water. Conducts better than fresh and freezes later.
Corroded, but iron still carries a charge.
Slow, thick and very willing to burn.
Catches from almost nothing and burns out fast.
Still hot. Water poured on it comes back up as steam.
Wet AND flammable — the one tile that answers to either school.
Breathes cold. Standing water near it will not stay liquid.
Frozen water still carries a charge — and it is brittle.
Wet and hot at once. Carries charge like the water it came from.
Oak, banded, and full of something. It will not go in a pack, but it will go across a floor.
A wheel of grey stone with a square hole through the middle. Off its spindle it is just a very heavy circle.
Not hard to move because it is heavy. Hard to move because there is nowhere to hold it.
A lidded box cut from one block. Whoever put it here did not expect it to leave.
A roof timber, down and lying where it landed. One end is charred.
Kept, and heavy with it. The salt has taken up residence in every part that used to be soft.
A wall of hawthorn and bramble, laid and woven by somebody's grandparents. It marks a boundary that no longer has a court to argue it.
Barley, planted in the old strips. Someone is coming back for this.
Packed earth over old stone, rutted by cartwheels. It goes somewhere, which is more than most things here do.
Pale bells on thin stems, growing where nobody sowed them. They are said to keep. Nobody in the Spread can tell you what they keep away.
Petals someone hummed up for the season, a carved token half-buried underneath for whichever river-god still gets the offerings here. It won't last.
A worn stone by the water, carved tokens left in its lap for whichever river-god still gets the offerings here. The Tree is a children's story in a place like this.
The pan cracked into plates as it dried. The ridges are sharp enough to read by.
Soft sand stacked steeper than it looks. Easier to go around than over.
Picked clean and dried white. Whatever it was, it was walking the road.
A big banded lizard basking flat on the crust, all display and speed. It holds its ground like it owns the noon.
A grey briar that grows where nothing should, its leaves rimed with the pan's own salt. Caravans strip it as they pass.
Woven goat-hair, dense enough to keep the noon out. The wall of a house that moves.
A dark cloth on a straight pole, hung where it can be seen from a long way off. What it offers holds for three days. Anyone following you knows what it means.
Weathered, unhurried, watching the road the way a well-keeper watches the water level.
A planed board in the Concord's neat hand: WE CANNOT GUARANTEE DELIVERY BEYOND THIS POINT. Underneath, older and fainter, the same words twice more.
White to the elbows. The scales beside the ledger are cleaner than anything else in the camp.
Tea-dark and still. It holds what it takes; the bog country is patient that way.
Planks laid on posts over the soft ground, worn smooth down the middle. Some of them answer your weight.
Grey wood standing in the water it drowned in. It kept its shape better than its neighbors.
Cut peat, the tool marks still clean. The bank face is layered like a book nobody meant to write.
A body the peat kept. Tanned dark as the water that took it; the knot in its cloak-cord is still a knot. It was not buried. It fell, and the bog wrote it down.

Older than the peat that holds it, and whole to the fingernails. A tin tag on waxed cord, Palimpsest work: 'Recension XI. Body-reading yields: leaf-light through high rooms; a name spoken to a tree, and answered. Reading incomplete.' The attribution is the expedition's. The body says nothing.
Fat, green, and unbothered until you are close enough to matter. The peat-cutters render them for lamp oil and know which pools they breed in, and guard that knowing like money.
Banded scarlet over black, and the bands are not decoration. Everything in the bog knows not to touch it; the lesson is the skin.
Mostly mouth. It sits where the dead trees stand in the water and it does not chase, because it has never needed to.
A bent stem strung with beads of something clearer than water. The beads do not fall. What it holds, it holds gently, and for exactly as long as it pleases; what it lets go walks away thinner.
Rendered fat in a stoppered gourd. Burns slow, smells like the bog it came from. Sumphold lamps run on it.
A hull upside-down on trestles, ribs bare, seams waiting for pitch. Sumphold builds shallow and wide, for water that is mostly patience.

Bound crossing-counts under a rain-hood, a century deep and mould-spotted: carts, heads, coin, initials. One entry is pressed harder than the rest of its year: short count -- forgiven -- my error. The rolls do not record a face.
A numbered stake, paint gone grey. The numbering starts somewhere out of sight and does not appear to be close to done.

A long table under canvas, scrubbed pale. Straps, padded blocks, a folio stand: everything arranged so a body may be read without being moved more than it must be. The attending junior's stool sits where the light is worst.
Ink to the second knuckle, and a table of attributions never out of reach. Reads everything twice; asserts almost nothing.
Gloves, always. A ledger of numbered things, each entry ending in the same word. Handles everything as if it were on loan, which, per the files, it is.
Boots to the thigh and a blade like a long spade worn to a shine. Smells of smoke that never quite goes out.

Wrapped, waxed, and corded to Curation intake standard; the sorter's stamp is in the seal. The label, in a careful hand: one entry. Status: continuing. It is heavier than it looks, and it looks heavy.
The intake window of Marrowstye is a person at a table, and the person is this one. Stamps in a row, wax in a warmer, and a ledger whose every entry ends the same way.
A column of pale growth, waist-thick and faintly warm, veined violet under the skin. The light in the veins moves slowly, always in the same direction. It holds up nothing. It is not for holding up.
Clean water rising cold through white filaments, clearer than any well in the towns. The sign says it is for you. Nothing here has ever said otherwise.
Growth in shelves and closed fists, violet over ochre. It was not this size last season. It will not be this size next season.

A board of grown wood, the letters raised in living grain — grown out of it, not carved into it — and weathered smooth by hands. It reads: WALKER. YOU ARE ENTERING US. Walk anywhere. Everything is path. Drink at the seep. It is for you. Eat nothing red. The red is thinking. If you hear singing, it is old singing. It is not for you. You may listen anyway. The singers do not mind. The singers have not minded anything for a long time, and it is a kindness to be heard. Do not dig. If you are tired — truly tired, walker, the kind of tired that has stopped keeping count — lie down anywhere soft. Someone will cover you. If you are only a little tired, keep walking. We can tell the difference. We are patient about the difference. GO GENTLY. EVERYTHING HERE IS SOMEBODY.

A tidy row of what is being taken back: cloth gone to lace, a boot, chitin, a shape further along than the rest. The rows are straight. Nothing made them straight; they grew that way. Everything here is somebody.
